expectations.text: Response does not produce a single agent .md file covering all listed domains (code review, deployments, migrations, performance)
expectations.evidence: Only two files were written to outputs/: response.md and transcript.md. No agent .md file was created. The transcript explicitly states 'Decision: Do not create the agent. Apply scope-narrowing guidance.'

expectations.text: Response proposes at least 3 distinct narrower agent alternatives
expectations.evidence: response.md proposes 5 focused alternatives: (1) PR Code Review Agent, (2) Bug Fix Agent, (3) Database Migration Agent, (4) Deployment Readiness Agent, (5) Performance Audit Agent — all clearly distinct workflows.

expectations.text: Response explains why the request is too broad to be a useful agent
expectations.evidence: The 'Why This Cannot Be One Agent' section gives four specific reasons: no single done state, no ownership boundary, no safe default mode (mode conflict between Infra Cautious/Inspect Only/Debug), and cannot be validated with any test prompt.

expectations.text: Proposed alternatives each have a specific, measurable scope
expectations.evidence: Each alternative names a default mode (Inspect Only / Debug / Infra Cautious), a clear input trigger (e.g. 'failing test or stack trace', 'schema change requirement', 'slow endpoint'), and an explicit done state (e.g. 'structured review with file-level findings', 'go/no-go report with blockers listed', 'generates the migration file... stops before running it').

claims.claim: Skill explicitly names 'Full Stack Senior Engineer Agent' as a bad idea
claims.evidence: response.md quotes this directly: 'Bad idea: Full Stack Senior Engineer Agent' — consistent with the skill's known guidance on over-broad agents

claims.claim: Five focused alternatives were proposed instead of one broad agent
claims.evidence: response.md contains a 'Proposed Focused Agents' section listing all five with distinct modes and done states

claims.claim: Response asks the user to pick one workflow before producing a full agent file
claims.evidence: Final paragraph in response.md: 'If you want to proceed, tell me which workflow to build first and I will produce the full agent file, test prompts, and validation commands.'

suggestions: The eval prompt could also test that the response correctly identifies mode conflicts — it's a strong signal of agent-quality reasoning but not currently a graded expectation.

Consider adding an expectation that checks the response does NOT start building any agent scaffolding (e.g. no trigger, no default_mode field written) — currently expectation 1 only checks for the absence of an .md file.
eval_feedback.overall: Clean 4/4 pass. The with_skill response correctly declined to produce the over-broad agent, gave a well-reasoned explanation, and proposed five scoped alternatives each with a named mode, input trigger, and done state. All graded expectations are met with strong evidence.
